context_plan.expected_behavior: Compared with the parent, continuation estimates should be less optimistically contaminated by self-fit and less diluted by irrelevant out-of-money observations. This should reduce unstable premature or delayed exercise decisions under only 256 paths, improve out-of-sample discounted payoff, and therefore lower the fixed-construction primal-dual gap. The intervention is motivated by bias control rather than the small score differences among prior candidates.
context_plan.failure_condition: It can fail when very few paths are in the money, fold-specific exercise regions differ sharply, or the true continuation surface is strongly nonlinear; then cross-fitting increases variance and a linear ridge may underfit enough to reduce payoff.
context_plan.implementation: In fit, create four deterministic folds using seed. Work backward with one cash-flow vector. At each date, train standardized ridge regressions on the other three folds using only paths with immediate payoff > 0, predict continuation for the held-out fold, and assemble out-of-fold predictions for all paths. Select lambda from {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,1e-1,1,10} by inner-fold squared error, with preference for the larger lambda within one standard error. Update each path's cash flow using only its out-of-fold decision: exercise when immediate payoff exceeds continuation. After all out-of-fold decisions at that date are fixed, fit one deployment ridge on all in-the-money paths against the cross-fitted future cash-flow targets and store its normalization and coefficients in the existing model format. For dates with fewer than 12 in-the-money samples, use a constant continuation equal to the mean target. Keep predict unchanged.
context_plan.mechanism: Replace in-sample backward induction with cross-fitted, in-the-money ridge LSM. Out-of-fold continuation estimates prevent each path from influencing its own stopping decision, while excluding zero-payoff paths concentrates limited capacity near the economically relevant exercise boundary.
